newsitem.title: USA: U S West seeks to serve all of Minnesota.
newsitem.headline: U S West seeks to serve all of Minnesota.

text.p: U S West Communications Group said Friday it asked the Minnesota Public Utilities Commission to give consumers increased choice in long-distance companies by opening up the entire state to long-distance competition by all providers.
Currently, U S West is forbidden from providing long-distance service beyond the boundaries of small geographic areas called Local Access Transport Areas (LATAs).
Today, there are five LATA's in Minnesota. U S West's proposal would consolidate the five to make the entire state one LATA.

"The over 120 long distance providers in Minnesota today are proof that competition exists," said Jim Smiley, U S West vice president-Minnesota. "Consolidating LATAs will foster the pro-competitive policies of the commission and the 1996 Telecommunications Act passed by Congress earlier this year."
